q: How many books are in the Bible?
why: 39 in the Old Testament, 27 in the New.

q: Who was thrown into the lions’ den?
why: Daniel, for praying when a new law forbade it.

q: What did God create on the first day?
why: Light — the sun does not appear until day four.

q: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
why: Twelve — one for each tribe of Israel.

q: What did David use against Goliath?
why: A sling and five smooth stones, having refused Saul’s armour.

q: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
why: Jonah, running from God’s call to Nineveh.

q: Which book opens the New Testament?
why: Matthew — though Mark was probably written first.

q: How long was Jesus in the tomb?
why: Three days, counted inclusively — part of Friday, Saturday, part of Sunday.

q: Who wrote most of the New Testament letters?
why: Paul — thirteen letters carry his name.

q: Which city did Jonah refuse to go to?
why: Nineveh, the capital of the empire that terrorised Israel.
